original_question: When virtual crossings are added to the Temperley-Lieb algebra so that the resulting algebra becomes the Brauer algebra of all connections from n points to n points, what is the structure of the Jones-Wenzl projectors in that setting, and can one formulate a useful algebraic generalization of classical recoupling theory there?
target_in_paper: Section 7, Problem 14 ("Brauer algebra"): the open problem asking for the structure of Jones-Wenzl projectors in the Brauer algebra obtained by adjoining virtual crossings to Temperley-Lieb, and for a virtual/algebraic generalization of classical recoupling theory. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper's actual problem: it identifies the passage from Temperley-Lieb to the Brauer algebra by adjoining virtual crossings, keeps the description in terms of all connections from n points to n points, asks about the Jones-Wenzl projectors in that enlarged algebra, and asks whether one can build an algebraic generalization of classical recoupling theory there. Those are exactly the two questions posed in Problem 14. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
missing_details: The paper frames this specifically as Problem 14 under the heading "Brauer algebra" and says that this is the appropriate setting for "virtual recoupling theory"; your draft captures the substance but not that framing. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper uses the intermediate name "Virtual Temperley Lieb Algebra" for Temperley-Lieb with virtual crossings before identifying the resulting algebra with the Brauer algebra of all n-to-n connection diagrams. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper does not specify a base ring, parameter choice, or a full presentation by generators and relations for this Brauer/virtual Temperley-Lieb algebra in Problem 14, so a faithful rewrite should not add such data. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))

The paper also does not formalize the projector axioms to be imposed in the Brauer setting, nor does it define a precise criterion for when the generalized recoupling theory is "useful"; those ambiguities are part of the open problem itself. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
refined_question: Let B_n denote the Brauer algebra obtained by adjoining virtual crossings to the Temperley-Lieb algebra on n boundary points, so that B_n is the diagram algebra of all connection patterns from n points to n points (the paper's "Virtual Temperley Lieb Algebra"). What is the structure of the Jones-Wenzl projectors when placed in B_n, and can these projectors be used to formulate a virtual analogue of the classical Temperley-Lieb recoupling theory in this Brauer-algebra setting? ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
justification: The nearest official formulation is not a conjecture or theorem but the verbatim open problem in Section 7, Problem 14. The introduction says the paper's later section is a list of specific problems, and Section 4 gives the relevant nearby context by explaining that three-manifold invariants are formulated using quantum algebras and spin recoupling networks; this explains why Problem 14 is naturally about recoupling theory rather than a broader representation-theoretic program. The refinement therefore stays narrow: it keeps the Brauer-algebra enlargement of Temperley-Lieb, the Jones-Wenzl projectors, and the goal of a virtual/generalized recoupling theory, while avoiding extra assumptions not supplied by the paper. No explicit equivalent reformulation is stated or proved near this problem, so no alternate version should be introduced. ([ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn](https://ymsc.tsinghua.edu.cn/__local/9/84/D5/2B246EB7EE7966BCCB35D74B76D_AAB7F286_40CAA.pdf))
